dims.what: Game rules: only outcomes, requirements, items, units, captains and numbers in the facts; nothing the game can't do
dims.reason: Every outcome, requirement, item (HealthRestore), unit (Swordsman, Sniper), captain (Conqueror) and number exists in the facts and stays inside the guardrails: SquallLine -70 ship equals shipLossMax, Mutterings Captain -50 equals crewDeltaMax, TallyRock +120 gold is under 150 and 80 XP equals xpMax. Captain -50 floors at 1, so no event can kill. The ungated Recruit choices are already deducted by code. Weakest remaining rules point: LoseCrew Random in MutteringsBelowDeck choices[2] has no CrewCountAtLeast gate, so on a captain-only crew that branch silently does nothing (S04).

dims.what: Text matches data: every body, label and result is true to the outcomes of its choice, in every RandomOf branch (V07)
dims.reason: Most text maps to data (V07). TallyRock 'pocket half the coin' matches Gold +60 against the strongbox's +120. SquallLine's single RandomOf result 'Whatever the sea took, it took fast' reads true for both -10 and -70. Weakest line: the DesertersLongboat label 'Trade rations for medicine' promises rations, but the data spends only Gold -20. The result half-admits this ('a sack of hardtack and a few coins'), so the label still misleads. Mutterings 'By morning, the crew has settled it their own way' is true in both branches but hides a permanent LoseCrew (see voice/S04). 'Whether there's a bunk to spare is another matter' admits the full-crew no-op but doesn't make it true.

dims.what: Real decisions with sink-or-plunder tension (S02), ship vs crew costs (S03), Good/Bad fit (S07), fair for a medium ~30 minute run, no dominant or trap choice
dims.reason: SquallLine and Mutterings are strong. SquallLine makes you choose between the hull and the crew (S03): ship -45, crew -20 All plus ship -15, or a 50/50 of ship -10/-70. Mutterings sets gold against the captain's health against a 1-in-3 permanent loss, and both Bad events offer a choice that limits the damage (S07). The two Good events have no sink-or-plunder tension (S02). TallyRock is three free gains: 'Open the strongbox' (+120 gold) or 'Read the notes aloud' (60 XP All), with no cost or risk anywhere. DesertersLongboat sets a free recruit (shop value 80) against 2 HealthRestore for 20 gold (shop value 60). With a crew of 3 the recruit nearly always wins, and with a crew of 4 it is a trap (already deducted).

dims.what: Sounds like the voice rules (V01-V07), the reference lines and the shipped pool; Ship's Log aesthetic (A01-A03)
dims.reason: The voice is dry and concrete and matches the reference lines (V02, V03): 'Old coin, still dry. Whoever left it isn't coming back for it.' and 'Coin goes around the deck and the muttering stops. For now.' Weakest line: Mutterings choices[1].resultText 'The captain takes the ringleader on in front of everyone' drops into third person and breaks V01's 'you'. The Mutterings LoseCrew branch never names who goes (S04's 'lets it land'). SquallLine's 'You have a minute to decide how to take it.' is flat filler, and 'until their hands bleed' repeats the shipped SomethingUnderTheKeel line.

dims.what: Stranger test: could a stranger tell this is Deadwater Run? Low if the event would work unchanged in any other pirate game (S01-S08, C01-C03)
dims.reason: Uneven. TallyRock is built on this game: crews that sailed on to the Kraken (S06), the rival crews' run (S08), and a Conqueror gate that plays to C03 ('You'll be the one ending it'). DesertersLongboat leans on the Swordsman/Sniper roster and the 4-crew cap (S05) plus rival-ship deserters (S08). Weakest: SquallLine ('The horizon goes black from end to end.') and Mutterings ('Too many fights and too few shares have soured the crew.') are a storm and a mutiny from any pirate game. Only the ship/crew split (S03) and the unnamed LoseCrew (S04) tie them to Deadwater Run.
